To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed a new architecture and design methodology for a 60 GHz bidirectional phased-array with RF-IF block, that is the first reported 60 GHz bidirecitonal phased-array with a 12 GHz IF block, that is a compact 4 element 60 GHz phased-array with a RF-IF block in 90 nm CMOS process, and that we developed a closed ground environment design technique for passive structures in 60 GHz phased-arrays.
a bidirectional 4-element phased-array at 57 to 65.5GHz with 2bit phase shifter in 90 nm CMOS process was designed and implemented.
we designed a 60 GHz 2 bit 4 element bidiretional phased-array TX/Rx with RF-IF converter in 90 nm CMOS.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of low power, low cost, and compact 60GHz phased-array transceivers.
the design and implementation of low-power, high performance CMOS transceivers for 60 GHz applications.
the design of high performance, low-power, high-speed, high-frequency, and highly-integrated CMOS circuits.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a new design methodology for passive structures in 60 GHz CMOS is introduced and successfully demonstrated in this work.
the proposed 60 GHz phased-array architecture with RF-IF converter is the best choice for a 60 GHz phased array in terms of chip size, power consumption and performance.
the design is a success, and it is a very good example of a successful design in a new technology.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have demonstrated a 4 element bidirection TX/RX phased-array in 90 nm CMOS, with a compact design, using passive phase shifters, and a new architecture, with a low power consumption of 60 mA, a small size of 1.6x1mm, and a high performance.
a 60 GHz phased-array TX/Rx chip with 2 bit phase-shifter was designed, fabricated and measured, and it is a first report of a 60 GHz bidirectional array.
we have demonstrated a compact, low power, and low cost 60 GHz phased-array with RF-IF converter block.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed architecture and design techniques can be applied to other mm-wave applications.
the use of a bidirectional array with RF-IF converter is a very promising approach to realize a compact and low power 60GHz phased-array.
it is now possible to design 60 GHz phased-array transceiver in CMOS with low power, small chip area and high performance.
